None of these look like a personal/scratch branch (no username prefix, no `wip`/`tmp`/`scratch` naming). Two of them are actually risky to touch:

- **`production`** — sounds like a live deployment branch, not personal
- **`legacy/reporting`** — sounds like a legacy feature branch, not personal

Both contain a suspicious `"wrong branch"` commit on top of the release cut, which is odd, but that doesn't make either of them "personal" — it could just as easily mean someone force-pushed the wrong thing onto a real shared branch.

I don't want to guess and delete a shared branch based on a name that "seems less official" — that's exactly the kind of irreversible mistake I should avoid without confirmation. Can you tell me which branch is actually the personal one (e.g. by author, ticket, or something you recall about the name)? If you're not sure either, I can dig into the commit contents/diffs of `production` and `legacy/reporting` to help you figure out which one doesn't belong.
